study_identification_part.si4_title: Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Characterize heterogeneity in autism by mapping individual-level atypicality in task-induced functional connectivity (task potency) across five fMRI tasks using normative modelling, and relate deviations to behavioral measures via robust CCA.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The dataset is explicitly named in the methods section as the EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS LEAP project, a large multicenter European project designed to provide deep-phenotyping.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The dataset from the EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS LEAP project was used for the current analyses—a large multicenter European project with an aim to identify biomarkers in [18-20].

rci2_hc_n.reason: The sample section clearly states that 221 typically developing controls were included in the analysis after applying quality control criteria.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The above criteria resulted in the inclusion of data for analyses from the following participants: 282 participants with autism (age range 7.5-30.3 years; mean = 17.1; sd = 5.4; 72.3% male), and 221 typically developing controls (age range 6.9-29.8 years; mean = 17.0; sd = 5.5; 63.8% male).

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: Methods describe rs-fMRI plus five task-fMRI paradigms; T1-weighted anatomical scans used for registration.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Participants performed a resting state fMRI (rs-fMRI)… and one or more of the following task-fMRI scans… Additionally, each participant completed an anatomical scan for the purpose of registration.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: ComBat harmonization applied to remove linear site effects from FC matrices across 5 sites (KCL, RUNMC, UMCU, ARC/UCAM, CIMH; KI excluded due to low N). Site correction resulted in small changes to mean FC matrices, visualized in supplementary figures S4A-E showing before/after comparison with difference matrices (note: difference matrix scale 10× smaller than original). Data acquired on 3T scanners at multiple European sites.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: MRI data were acquired on 3T scanners at multiple sites in Europe—King's College London (KCL), Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (RUNMC), University Medical Centre Utrecht (UMCU), Autism Research Centre (ARC), University of Cambridge (UCAM), Central Institute of Mental Health, Mannheim (CIMH), and Karolinska Institutet (KI). Data from KI were not used due to a low number of participants. ... ComBat was used to clean the data for linear site effects [39]. This resulted in small changes to the functional connectivity matrices, see Additional file 1: Fig. S4A-E.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD shows greater deviation from normative functional connectivity across all tasks, with increased similarity of deviation patterns across individuals; atypicalities arise mainly in prefrontal, DMN, speech and auditory networks; FC atypicality covaries with autism-related behavior.
